papers.title: Bayesian optimisation for fast approximate inference in state-space models with intractable likelihoods
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of approximate Bayesian parameter inference in non-linear state-space models with intractable likelihoods. Sequential Monte Carlo with approximate Bayesian computations (SMC-ABC) is one approach to approximate the likelihood in this type of models. However, such approximations can be noisy and computationally costly which hinders efficient implementations using standard methods based on optimisation and Monte Carlo methods. We propose a computationally efficient novel method based on the combination of Gaussian process optimisation and SMC-ABC to create a Laplace approximation of the intractable posterior. We exemplify the proposed algorithm for inference in stochastic volatility models with both synthetic and real-world data as well as for estimating the Value-at-Risk for two portfolios using a copula model. We document speed-ups of between one and two orders of magnitude compared to state-of-the-art algorithms for posterior inference.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种基于贝叶斯优化的近似推理方法，但应用于状态空间模型而非有限元代理建模，与用户的研究方向相关性较低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA sampling efficiency, constraint handling, uncertainty quantification for biomechanical simulations, or implant design; it focuses on statistical inference for state-space models with intractable likelihoods.

summary_zh.method: 结合高斯过程优化和SMC-ABC构建拉普拉斯近似
summary_zh.result: 相比现有算法加速1-2个数量级
summary_zh.validation: 通过随机波动率模型和VaR算例验证

summary_en.motivation: To achieve computationally efficient approximate Bayesian inference in nonlinear state-space models with intractable likelihoods.
summary_en.method: A novel method combining Gaussian process optimization with sequential Monte Carlo approximate Bayesian computation (SMC-ABC) to construct a Laplace approximation of the intractable posterior.
summary_en.result: The proposed method achieves speed-ups of one to two orders of magnitude over state-of-the-art algorithms for posterior inference.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on synthetic and real-world data for stochastic volatility models and for estimating Value-at-Risk using copula models.

papers.title: Burr-like, laser-made 3D microscaffolds for tissue spheroid encagement.
papers.abstract: The modeling, fabrication, cell loading, and mechanical and in vitro biological testing of biomimetic, interlockable, laser-made, concentric 3D scaffolds are presented. The scaffolds are made by multiphoton polymerization of an organic-inorganic zirconium silicate. Their mechanical properties are theoretically modeled using finite elements analysis and experimentally measured using a Microsquisher(®). They are subsequently loaded with preosteoblastic cells, which remain live after 24 and 72 h. The interlockable scaffolds have maintained their ability to fuse with tissue spheroids. This work represents a novel technological platform, enabling the rapid, laser-based, in situ 3D tissue biofabrication.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文未涉及AI或机器学习方法，与生物打印中AI的应用方向无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not incorporate AI/ML into any bioprinting workflow stage, lacks experimental validation of AI models, and does not advance toward autonomous decision-making.

summary_zh.motivation: 制造用于组织球体融合的仿生互锁3D支架。
summary_zh.method: 使用多光子聚合制备锆硅酸盐支架，并进行有限元模拟和力学测试。
summary_zh.result: 支架具有互锁能力，细胞存活良好。
summary_zh.validation: 力学测试和体外细胞实验。

summary_en.motivation: To fabricate biomimetic interlockable 3D scaffolds for tissue spheroid encagement.
summary_en.method: Multiphoton polymerization of zirconium silicate combined with finite element modeling and mechanical testing.
summary_en.result: Scaffolds maintained integrity and supported cell viability.
summary_en.validation: Microsquisher mechanical tests and in vitro cell assays.
